records.source: וַיִּסַּ֨ע מִשָּׁ֤ם אַבְרָהָם֙ אַ֣רְצָה הַנֶּ֔גֶב וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בֵּין־קָדֵ֖שׁ וּבֵ֣ין שׁ֑וּר וַיָּ֖גָר בִּגְרָֽר׃
records.gloss: And journeyed from there Abraham toward [the] land of the Negev, and dwelt between Kadesh and between Shur, and sojourned in Gerar.
pieces: Abraham set out from there toward the southern country of the Negev. He settled between Kadesh and Shur, and for a time he lived as a foreigner in Gerar.

L.1: And Abraham journeyed from there toward the land of the Negev and settled between Kadesh and Shur; and he sojourned in Gerar.

R.1: Abraham left there and traveled south into the dry land of the Negev. He lived between Kadesh and Shur. For a while he stayed in the town of Gerar as an outsider.

decisions.choice: from there: from Mamre, near Hebron
decisions.reason: Abraham had been living by the oaks of Mamre (13:18; 18:1). He now moves south toward the edge of the desert.

decisions.choice: the Negev: the dry south country
decisions.reason: The Negev is the dry land south of Hebron, between the hill country and the Sinai desert. Kadesh and Shur mark its southern and western edges (16:7, 14). Gerar lay in its western part, toward Gaza (10:19; 26:1).

decisions.choice: sojourned (gur): lived as a resident foreigner
decisions.reason: The verb means to live in a place without belonging to it, without the rights of a citizen or land of one's own. Abraham is a sojourner in the land promised to him (23:4).

decisions.choice: lived as a foreigner (B), stayed ... as an outsider (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what kind of stay this was (m3).

records.source: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר אַבְרָהָ֛ם אֶל־שָׂרָ֥ה אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ אֲחֹ֣תִי הִ֑וא וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח אֲבִימֶ֨לֶךְ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ גְּרָ֔ר וַיִּקַּ֖ח אֶת־שָׂרָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Abraham concerning Sarah his wife, my sister [is] she. And sent Abimelech, king of Gerar, and took Sarah.
pieces: There Abraham said of his wife Sarah, "She is my sister." So Abimelech, the king of Gerar, sent men to fetch Sarah and took her into his household.

L.2: And Abraham said of Sarah his wife, "She is my sister." And Abimelech king of Gerar sent and took Sarah.

R.2: Abraham told people that his wife Sarah was his sister. So Abimelech, the king of Gerar, sent for Sarah and took her into his household.

decisions.choice: She is my sister: the same deception as in Egypt
decisions.reason: Abraham had said the same of Sarah in Egypt, and Pharaoh had taken her (12:11-20). Sarah was in fact his half-sister (verse 12), but the words were meant to hide that she was his wife. The danger now falls just before the promised son is born (18:10; 21:2).

decisions.choice: sent and took: took her as a wife
decisions.reason: A king could take a woman into his household as one of his wives (verse 3, 'the woman whom you have taken'). Sarah is about ninety (17:17); the text gives no reason for the king's choice, and such a marriage could also serve to bind a wealthy newcomer to the king.

decisions.choice: sent men to fetch Sarah and took her into his household (B); sent for Sarah and took her into his household (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only that he sent and took her; Balanced and Readable say where she was taken (m2).

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֧א אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶל־אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ בַּחֲל֣וֹם הַלָּ֑יְלָה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ הִנְּךָ֥ מֵת֙ עַל־הָאִשָּׁ֣ה אֲשֶׁר־לָקַ֔חְתָּ וְהִ֖וא בְּעֻ֥לַת בָּֽעַל׃
records.gloss: And came God to Abimelech in a dream of the night and said to him, behold, you [are] dying because of the woman whom you have taken, and she [is] married to a husband.
pieces: But that night God came to Abimelech in a dream. "You are as good as dead," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told him, "because of the woman you have taken. She already has a husband."

L.3: But God came to Abimelech in a dream by night and said to him, "Look, you are a dead man because of the woman whom you have taken, for she is married to a husband."

R.3: But God came to Abimelech in a dream that night. God said, "You are going to die because of the woman you took. She is another man's wife."

decisions.choice: you are a dead man: you are under sentence of death
decisions.reason: The word is a participle, 'dying': as far as God is concerned the sentence is already passed. Verse 7 shows it can still be lifted if Sarah is returned.

decisions.choice: married to a husband: legally another man's wife
decisions.reason: The phrase (be'ulat ba'al) means a woman who belongs to a husband. Taking another man's wife was a capital offense in Israel's later law (Leviticus 20:10; Deuteronomy 22:22).

decisions.choice: God came to Abimelech in a dream: God speaks to a foreign king
decisions.reason: God speaks directly to a king outside Abraham's family and protects Sarah, the mother of the promised son, when Abraham himself does not.

records.source: וַאֲבִימֶ֕לֶךְ לֹ֥א קָרַ֖ב אֵלֶ֑יהָ וַיֹּאמַ֕ר אֲדֹנָ֕י הֲג֥וֹי גַּם־צַדִּ֖יק תַּהֲרֹֽג׃
records.gloss: And Abimelech had not come near to her. And he said, Lord, a nation even righteous will you kill?
pieces: Abimelech had not touched her. He said, "Lord, would {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put to death a people who have done no wrong?

L.4: Now Abimelech had not come near her. And he said, "Lord, will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} kill a nation even [if it is] righteous?

R.4: Abimelech had not had sex with Sarah. He said, "Lord, will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} kill people who have done nothing wrong?

decisions.choice: had not come near her: had not had sexual relations with her
decisions.reason: To 'come near' a woman is a polite way of speaking of sexual relations (Leviticus 18:6).

decisions.choice: Lord (Adonai): a title of respect
decisions.reason: Abimelech addresses God as 'my Lord', a title, not the divine name. He speaks to God respectfully, though he does not yet know who he is dealing with.

decisions.choice: will you kill a righteous nation?: Abraham's own question
decisions.reason: Abraham had asked of Sodom, 'Will you sweep away the righteous with the wicked?' (18:23-25). Now a foreign king asks the same question, about Abraham's wrong. 'Nation' means the king and his people, who would share his punishment (verse 9).

records.source: הֲלֹ֨א ה֤וּא אָֽמַר־לִי֙ אֲחֹ֣תִי הִ֔וא וְהִֽיא־גַם־הִ֥וא אָֽמְרָ֖ה אָחִ֣י ה֑וּא בְּתָם־לְבָבִ֛י וּבְנִקְיֹ֥ן כַּפַּ֖י עָשִׂ֥יתִי זֹֽאת׃
records.gloss: Did not he say to me, my sister [is] she? And she, even she said, my brother [is] he. In [the] integrity of my heart and in [the] innocence of my palms I have done this.
pieces: It was he who told me, 'She is my sister,' and she herself said, 'He is my brother.' My heart was honest and my hands were innocent when I did this."

L.5: Did he not himself say to me, 'She is my sister'? And she, she herself said, 'He is my brother.' In the integrity of my heart and the innocence of my hands I have done this."

R.5: Abraham told me, 'She is my sister.' And Sarah said, 'He is my brother.' I meant no harm, and I have done nothing wrong."

decisions.choice: the integrity of my heart and the innocence of my hands: right intentions and clean actions
decisions.reason: The heart stands for the intention and the hands for the deed. Abimelech claims that both were blameless (Psalm 24:4). God agrees about the heart (verse 6).

decisions.choice: she herself said: Sarah took part
decisions.reason: The words are emphatic: Abraham said it, and Sarah said it too. She had agreed to the plan long before (verse 13).

decisions.choice: I meant no harm, and I have done nothing wrong
alternatives: in the integrity of my heart and the innocence of my hands
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the picture of heart and hands (m1).

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אֵלָ֨יו הָֽאֱלֹהִ֜ים בַּחֲלֹ֗ם גַּ֣ם אָנֹכִ֤י יָדַ֨עְתִּי֙ כִּ֤י בְתָם־לְבָבְךָ֙ עָשִׂ֣יתָ זֹּ֔את וָאֶחְשֹׂ֧ךְ גַּם־אָנֹכִ֛י אֽוֹתְךָ֖ מֵחֲטוֹ־לִ֑י עַל־כֵּ֥ן לֹא־נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לִנְגֹּ֥עַ אֵלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And said to him God in the dream, also I know that in [the] integrity of your heart you did this, and I also withheld you from sinning against me; therefore I did not let you touch her.
pieces: God answered him in the dream, "Yes, I know you acted with an honest heart, and it was I who held you back from sinning against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and so I gave you no chance to touch her.

L.6: And God said to him in the dream, "Yes, I know that you did this in the integrity of your heart, and it was I who kept you from sinning against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Therefore I did not let you touch her.

R.6: God said to him in the dream, "Yes, I know you did not mean to do wrong. And I stopped you from sinning against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. That is why I kept you away from her.

decisions.choice: I kept you from sinning against me: God holds a man back
decisions.reason: God claims the credit for Abimelech's innocence: he kept him from Sarah, probably by the illness that verses 17-18 describe. To take another man's wife is a sin against God himself (39:9; Psalm 51:4).

decisions.choice: touch her: have sexual relations with her
decisions.reason: 'Touch' is used here, as in Proverbs 6:29, as a polite word for sexual contact.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה הָשֵׁ֤ב אֵֽשֶׁת־הָאִישׁ֙ כִּֽי־נָבִ֣יא ה֔וּא וְיִתְפַּלֵּ֥ל בַּֽעַדְךָ֖ וֶֽחְיֵ֑ה וְאִם־אֵֽינְךָ֣ מֵשִׁ֗יב דַּ֚ע כִּי־מ֣וֹת תָּמ֔וּת אַתָּ֖ה וְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And now, return [the] wife of the man, for a prophet [is] he, and he will pray for you, and live; and if you [are] not returning [her], know that dying you will die, you and all who [are] to you.
pieces: Now give the man back his wife. He is a prophet, and he will pray for you so that you live. But if you do not return her, know for certain that death awaits you and everyone who belongs to you."

L.7: And now, return the man's wife, for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you, and you shall live. But if you do not return [her], know that you shall surely die, you and all who are yours."

R.7: Now give the man his wife back. He is a prophet. He will pray for you, and you will live. But if you do not give her back, you will certainly die. And so will all your people."

decisions.choice: prophet (navi): one who stands between God and others
decisions.reason: This is the first time the Bible uses the word. A prophet speaks for God, and also speaks to God for others. Here the point is prayer: Abraham will pray for the king (verse 17), as Moses and Samuel later prayed for Israel (Numbers 21:7; 1 Samuel 12:23).

decisions.choice: you shall surely die: the doubled verb
decisions.reason: The verb is repeated ('dying you will die') for certainty, as in God's warning in 2:17.

decisions.choice: all who are yours: the king's household and people
decisions.reason: A king's guilt falls on all who belong to him (verse 9, 'me and my kingdom').

records.source: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם אֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ בַּבֹּ֗קֶר וַיִּקְרָא֙ לְכָל־עֲבָדָ֔יו וַיְדַבֵּ֛ר אֶת־כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה בְּאָזְנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּֽירְא֥וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And rose early Abimelech in the morning and called all his servants and spoke all these words in their ears; and feared the men greatly.
pieces: Abimelech got up at dawn, called together all his officials and repeated all of this to them, and the men were badly frightened.

L.8: So Abimelech rose early in the morning and called all his servants and told all these things in their ears; and the men were very much afraid.

R.8: Early the next morning Abimelech called a meeting of all his officials. He told them about the dream, and fear came over them.

decisions.choice: his servants: the king's officials
decisions.reason: The word (eved) covers anyone under another's authority, from slaves to royal officers. The servants of a king are his court and officials.

decisions.choice: the men were very much afraid: foreigners who fear God
decisions.reason: Abraham assumed there was 'no fear of God in this place' (verse 11), yet the king and his men are afraid when God speaks.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: For a king's court Balanced and Readable say 'officials'; Literal keeps 'servants' (m1).

decisions.choice: about the dream
decisions.reason: Readable says what 'these things' were.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ לְאַבְרָהָ֗ם וַיֹּ֨אמֶר ל֜וֹ מֶֽה־עָשִׂ֤יתָ לָּ֨נוּ֙ וּמֶֽה־חָטָ֣אתִי לָ֔ךְ כִּֽי־הֵבֵ֧אתָ עָלַ֛י וְעַל־מַמְלַכְתִּ֖י חֲטָאָ֣ה גְדֹלָ֑ה מַעֲשִׂים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־יֵֽעָשׂ֔וּ עָשִׂ֖יתָ עִמָּדִֽי׃
records.gloss: And called Abimelech Abraham and said to him, what have you done to us? And how have I sinned against you, that you have brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin? Deeds that are not done you have done with me.
pieces: Then Abimelech sent for Abraham. "What have you done to us?" he said. "What wrong did I ever do you, that you should expose me and my kingdom to so great a sin? You have treated me in a way no one should ever be treated."

L.9: Then Abimelech called Abraham and said to him, "What have you done to us? And how have I sinned against you, that you have brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin? Deeds that ought not to be done you have done to me."

R.9: Then Abimelech called Abraham and said, "What have you done to us? Did I ever do you any harm? Because of you, I and my whole kingdom nearly committed a terrible sin. What you did to me was wrong!"

decisions.choice: a great sin: adultery
decisions.reason: Abimelech treats taking a married woman as a grave sin against God, not only a private wrong. In some writings from Egypt and Ugarit adultery is likewise called 'the great sin'.

decisions.choice: deeds that ought not to be done: what decent people do not do
decisions.reason: The phrase describes conduct that breaks the accepted rules of decency (29:26; 34:7). The foreign king rebukes the man of God.

decisions.choice: Because of you, I and my whole kingdom nearly committed
alternatives: you have brought on me ... a great sin
decisions.reason: Abimelech had not touched Sarah (verse 4), so Readable says the sin came close; the guilt was real enough that God threatened death (verse 3).

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ אֶל־אַבְרָהָ֑ם מָ֣ה רָאִ֔יתָ כִּ֥י עָשִׂ֖יתָ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Abimelech to Abraham, what did you see, that you have done this thing?
pieces: Abimelech pressed him: "What did you have in mind when you did this?"

L.10: And Abimelech said to Abraham, "What did you see, that you have done this thing?"

R.10: Abimelech asked Abraham, "Why did you do this?"

decisions.choice: what did you see: what was your reason?
decisions.reason: 'What did you see' asks what Abraham had in view, what he thought he saw in Gerar that made him act this way. His answer follows in verse 11.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַבְרָהָ֔ם כִּ֣י אָמַ֗רְתִּי רַ֚ק אֵין־יִרְאַ֣ת אֱלֹהִ֔ים בַּמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וַהֲרָג֖וּנִי עַל־דְּבַ֥ר אִשְׁתִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Abraham, for I said, surely there is not [the] fear of God in this place, and they will kill me on account of my wife.
pieces: Abraham answered, "I told myself that nobody here feared God, and that they would kill me to get my wife.

L.11: And Abraham said, "Because I thought, 'Surely there is no fear of God in this place, and they will kill me on account of my wife.'

R.11: Abraham answered, "I thought, 'The people here do not respect God at all. They will kill me so they can take my wife.'

decisions.choice: I thought: literally 'I said'
decisions.reason: 'I said' often means 'I said to myself', I thought (26:9).

decisions.choice: the fear of God: reverence that restrains from wrong
decisions.reason: To fear God is to respect him enough to keep his ways, especially toward the weak and the stranger (42:18; Exodus 1:17). Abraham judged Gerar wrongly: the king and his men did fear God (verse 8). In 22:12 the same words are said of Abraham.

records.source: וְגַם־אָמְנָ֗ה אֲחֹתִ֤י בַת־אָבִי֙ הִ֔וא אַ֖ךְ לֹ֣א בַת־אִמִּ֑י וַתְּהִי־לִ֖י לְאִשָּֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And also truly my sister, [the] daughter of my father [is] she, only not [the] daughter of my mother; and she became to me for a wife.
pieces: And in fact she is my sister: my father's daughter, though she had a different mother. Then she became my wife.

L.12: And besides, she is truly my sister, the daughter of my father, only not the daughter of my mother; and she became my wife.

R.12: Sarah really is my sister. Her father is my father, but her mother is not my mother. Then she became my wife.

decisions.choice: the daughter of my father, not of my mother: a half-sister
decisions.reason: Sarah was Terah's daughter by another wife; 11:29 does not name her parents. Marriage to a half-sister was later forbidden in Israel's law (Leviticus 18:9, 11; 20:17).

decisions.choice: she is truly my sister: a half-truth
decisions.reason: Abraham defends himself with what is true, but he used it to hide what was more important: that she was his wife. The excuse does not answer the king's charge.

records.source: וַיְהִ֞י כַּאֲשֶׁ֧ר הִתְע֣וּ אֹתִ֗י אֱלֹהִים֮ מִבֵּ֣ית אָבִי֒ וָאֹמַ֣ר לָ֔הּ זֶ֣ה חַסְדֵּ֔ךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשִׂ֖י עִמָּדִ֑י אֶ֤ל כָּל־הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה אִמְרִי־לִ֖י אָחִ֥י הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And it was, when caused me to wander God from the house of my father, and I said to her, this [is] your kindness which you will do with me: to every place where we come there, say of me, my brother [is] he.
pieces: When God sent me wandering away from my father's house, I asked her to prove her loyalty to me by saying, wherever we went, that I was her brother."

L.13: And when God caused me to wander from my father's house, I said to her, 'This is the kindness you shall do for me: in every place to which we come, say of me, "He is my brother."'"

R.13: God led me away from my father's home to wander from place to place. Back then I said to Sarah, 'If you are loyal to me, you will do this for me. Everywhere we go, tell people I am your brother.'"

decisions.choice: God caused me to wander: the verb is plural
decisions.reason: With 'God' (elohim) the verb is usually singular; here it is plural, as again in 35:7. Speaking to a foreign king, Abraham may use the general way of speaking about God or the gods. The verb 'wander' can describe roaming with no fixed home (21:14; Psalm 107:4).

decisions.choice: kindness (chesed): loyalty owed within a bond
decisions.reason: The word means the faithful love that people owe each other within a relationship, here a wife's loyalty to her husband (21:23; 24:12). Abraham asks Sarah to show it by sharing his deception.

decisions.choice: in every place: a standing plan
decisions.reason: Abraham reveals that the plan was made at the start of his travels. Egypt (12:13) and Gerar were not one-time lapses.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֨ח אֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ צֹ֣אן וּבָקָ֗ר וַעֲבָדִים֙ וּשְׁפָחֹ֔ת וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לְאַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיָּ֣שֶׁב ל֔וֹ אֵ֖ת שָׂרָ֥ה אִשְׁתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And took Abimelech sheep and cattle and male slaves and female slaves, and gave [them] to Abraham, and returned to him Sarah his wife.
pieces: Then Abimelech gave Abraham sheep and cattle and servants, both men and women, and he handed his wife Sarah back to him.

L.14: Then Abimelech took sheep and cattle, and male and female slaves, and gave [them] to Abraham; and he returned Sarah his wife to him.

R.14: Then Abimelech gave Abraham sheep, cattle and servants, both men and women. And he gave Sarah back to Abraham.

decisions.choice: the gifts: making amends in public
decisions.reason: Pharaoh had given gifts when he took Sarah and then sent Abraham away (12:16-20). Abimelech gives his gifts after returning her, to make amends and clear his own name.

decisions.choice: male and female slaves (eved, shifchah)
decisions.reason: These are people given as property, as in 12:16. The text reports the custom without approving it.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servants" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that they were owned, and Literal keeps "slaves".

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ הִנֵּ֥ה אַרְצִ֖י לְפָנֶ֑יךָ בַּטּ֥וֹב בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ שֵֽׁב׃
records.gloss: And said Abimelech, behold, my land [is] before you; in the good in your eyes dwell.
pieces: And Abimelech said, "My land lies open to you. Settle anywhere that pleases you."

L.15: And Abimelech said, "Look, my land is before you; dwell wherever it is good in your eyes."

R.15: Abimelech told him, "You can live anywhere you want in my land."

decisions.choice: my land is before you: an open welcome
decisions.reason: Pharaoh had expelled Abraham (12:19-20); Abimelech invites him to stay. Abraham offered Lot the same choice in 13:9.

records.source: וּלְשָׂרָ֣ה אָמַ֗ר הִנֵּ֨ה נָתַ֜תִּי אֶ֤לֶף כֶּ֨סֶף֙ לְאָחִ֔יךְ הִנֵּ֤ה הוּא־לָךְ֙ כְּס֣וּת עֵינַ֔יִם לְכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתָּ֑ךְ וְאֵ֥ת כֹּ֖ל וְנֹכָֽחַת׃
records.gloss: And to Sarah he said, behold, I have given a thousand of silver to your brother; behold, it [is] for you a covering of eyes for all who [are] with you, and with all, and you are vindicated.
pieces: To Sarah he said, "I have given your brother {{units:about 25 pounds|1,000 shekels}} of silver. Let it show everyone with you that you have done no wrong. In the eyes of all you are cleared."

L.16: And to Sarah he said, "Look, I have given your brother 1,000 [shekels] of silver. Look, it is for you a covering of the eyes before all who are with you, and before everyone you are vindicated."

R.16: Abimelech said to Sarah, "I am giving your brother {{units:about 25 pounds|1,000 shekels}} of silver. This will show everyone with you that you did nothing wrong. Everyone will know you are innocent."

decisions.choice: 1,000 of silver: a thousand shekels, a very large sum
decisions.reason: The unit is not named but is the shekel, a weight of about 0.4 ounce (11.5 grams), so the gift was about 25 pounds (11.5 kilograms) of silver. Abraham later pays 400 shekels for a field and a cave (23:15).

decisions.choice: a covering of the eyes: payment that clears her
alternatives: a gift to cover the offense
decisions.reason: The phrase is found only here. It most likely means compensation that covers others' eyes, so that no one can look on Sarah as disgraced. Abimelech pointedly calls Abraham 'your brother'.

decisions.choice: before everyone you are vindicated: an obscure ending
decisions.reason: The last words are difficult. The verb (yakach) means to settle a case, so the sense is probably that Sarah's case is decided in her favor before everyone.

decisions.choice: about 25 pounds; with the Measures setting, 1,000 shekels
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern weight by default and the original unit as the setting's alternative; Literal keeps the Hebrew '1,000 of silver' and supplies [shekels].

records.source: וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֥ל אַבְרָהָ֖ם אֶל־הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיִּרְפָּ֨א אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶת־אֲבִימֶ֧לֶךְ וְאֶת־אִשְׁתּ֛וֹ וְאַמְהֹתָ֖יו וַיֵּלֵֽדוּ׃
records.gloss: And prayed Abraham to God, and healed God Abimelech and his wife and his female slaves, and they bore.
pieces: Then Abraham prayed to God, and God restored Abimelech to health, and his wife and female servants too, and they were able to bear children.

L.17: Then Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech and his wife and his female slaves, and they bore children.

R.17: Abraham prayed to God. And God healed Abimelech, his wife and his female servants. Then children could be born in his household again.

decisions.choice: Abraham prayed: the prophet's work
decisions.reason: God had said that Abraham would pray for the king (verse 7). This is the first time the verb for prayer (palal) appears in the Bible. The man who caused the trouble is the one through whom healing comes.

decisions.choice: God healed ... and they bore children: the illness ended
decisions.reason: Verse 18 explains the illness: the women could not conceive. It may also have kept Abimelech from Sarah (verse 6).

decisions.choice: female servants
decisions.reason: "Female servants" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; Literal keeps "female slaves".

records.source: כִּֽי־עָצֹ֤ר עָצַר֙ יְהוָ֔ה בְּעַ֥ד כָּל־רֶ֖חֶם לְבֵ֣ית אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ עַל־דְּבַ֥ר שָׂרָ֖ה אֵ֥שֶׁת אַבְרָהָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: For closing YHWH had closed every womb of [the] household of Abimelech on account of Sarah, [the] wife of Abraham.
pieces: For on account of Abraham's wife Sarah, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had closed every womb in Abimelech's household.

L.18: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had completely closed every womb of the household of Abimelech because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.

R.18: That was because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had closed the womb of every woman in Abimelech's household. He did it because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.

decisions.choice: the LORD: the divine name for the first time in the chapter
decisions.reason: The chapter has spoken of 'God' throughout. In its last line the LORD, the God of the promise, appears by name: he guards Sarah, the mother of the son he promised, whose birth follows at once (21:1).

decisions.choice: closed every womb: the women could not have children
decisions.reason: The doubled verb stresses that it was complete. Opening and closing the womb are God's acts in Genesis (29:31; 30:22).
